messages:
jordan: Heads-up — customer on dedicated pool 'dedicated-gamma' reporting a sudden throughput drop and increased latency starting ~11:03 UTC. They're seeing 429s and longer tail latencies.

maya: I'm on the case, customer C-472. They sent logs, saying spikes coincide with bursts of long responses (several ~800 token completions).

liam: Any autoscaler events around that time? @sre-bot can you pull scheduler + autoscale metrics for 11:00-11:20?

sre-bot: Autoscaler: scale-out requested at 10:59, desired replicas +4, actual new replicas in service at 11:12. Node join delay ~13m. Also seeing kube-proxy restarts on ~2 nodes. Uploaded metrics bundle.

jordan: Thanks. Initial hunch: continuous-batcher queue depth ballooned, microbatches got tiny because long completions occupied token budget — inefficient packing. Might be a max_batch_tokens mismatch between route config and scheduler default.

maya: Customer reports intermittent 'queue timeout' errors then 429s. Their load profile: 300 rps for 2m with mix short(25t) / long(800t). I attached the sample request histogram.

liam: Can we get a quick repro script to validate? Ask them to run this against a non-prod replica:

```bash
# simple repro (curl)
for i in {1..300}; do
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"prompt":"lorem","max_tokens":800}' &
  sleep 0.003
 done
```

liam: Also need: service route config (max_batch_tokens), batch_fill_histogram, queue_depth, scheduler_latency.

jordan: Looked at route config for dedicated-gamma: max_batch_tokens=1024 but model profile default is 2048 for this model. Scheduler was treating requests as 2048-budget which caused packing fragmentation and lots of small microbatches.

liam: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) set max_batch_tokens=512 for that route, 2) enable per-tenant fair-queue weighting to reduce noisy-tenant dominance, 3) lower prefill_threshold to 0.4 to allow earlier microbatching. These are live-tunable.

maya: Can we apply those without rolling restarts? Customer needs ETA — they want fix within 30m.

jordan: Yes, runtime supports live config rollouts. I'll canary to a single node, monitor p95 and error rate.

sre-bot: Collected requested logs and histograms for 11:00-11:20 and uploaded: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1765432101/metrics.tar.gz

liam: After changing max_batch_tokens, watch effective fill_rate and average microbatch size. Expect fill_rate up, p95 latency down. If not, revert and try quota isolation.

sre-bot: Noted an autoscaler join failure root cause: kube-proxy flapping due to package version mismatch on new nodes in that AZ. Patch applied at 11:25.

maya: Customer says 429s stopped and latency normalized ~11:40.

jordan: :thumbsup: Rolling change successful on canary, promoted to pool at 11:32. Observed fill_rate +28%, microbatch count per request down 35%, p95 latency reduced from 620ms to 180ms.

liam: Filing follow-ups: ENG-3819 scheduler-token-mapping (ensure model profile alignment), SRE-4122 autoscaler-node-join-fix (prevent future kube-proxy flaps).

maya: Thanks all — I'll update the customer that we applied a live config change, autoscaler issue fixed, and we're tracking follow-up tickets. Marking thread resolved from support side.

ella: Quick note for postmortem: consider adding an alert on mismatch between route max_batch_tokens and model default token_budget. Saved time here.

jordan: Agreed. Adding to postmortem and closing the loop.
